definition: Privation means a lack of basic necessities.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word privation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know privation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The lighthouse posting meant a winter of privation: tinned food, brackish cistern water, and oil worth more than firewood.
A pinch is far milder than privation — a tight month where the budget groans but nothing essential is missing yet.
Starvation goes further than privation — privation is necessities running short; starvation is the body itself running out.

Want is the old, plain word for going without — 'families in want' — and it can stay general. Privation is sharper: what is missing are the basic necessities themselves, food, fuel, and light. Want says someone lacks; privation says they lack the essentials.

Hardship is difficulty of any kind — a brutal commute, a lawsuit, and a failed harvest all qualify. Privation is one particular hardship: life with the basic necessities gone. Every privation is a hardship, but a hardship only becomes privation when the pantry and the woodpile stand empty.
